newsitem.title: UK: BA still hopeful on American alliance.
newsitem.headline: BA still hopeful on American alliance.

text.p: British Airways Plc chairman Sir Colin Marshall told shareholders at the company's annual meeting on Tuesday he was still hopeful of securing BA's proposed alliance with American Airlines, despite protracted regulatory delays.

The proposed alliance, which was announced just over a year ago, has been held up by regulatory authorities in the UK, Europe and the U.S., as well as over talks about a new Anglo-U.S. aviation trade agreement.
"Approval for our alliance hangs on the problem of achieving greater access to a congested Heathrow for our transatlantic competitors," Marshall said.
"We are in continuing dialogue with the respective authorities and hopeful of a satisfactory outcome."
The main stumbling block for the "open skies" trade agreement has been in trying to satisfy U.S. demands for greater access to London's Heathrow airport.
